newsitem.title: USA: Several youths arrested in swastika investigation.
newsitem.headline: Several youths arrested in swastika investigation.

text.p: Eight people have been arrested for conducting a two-year racist campaign that including harassing black families and cutting a 60-foot (18-metre) swastika into a New Jersey corn field, officials said on Wednesday.

Two suspects, Jason Gancarz, 19, and Jefferey Harvey, 21, both of North Hanover, have been charged with criminal mischief, biased harassment and conspiracy in connection with the crime. They allegedly used machetes to create the swastika on July 20 on property in Mansfield belonging to a Jewish farmer.
The farmer lost thousands of dollars when he cut down surrounding corn plants before they were ready for harvest to erase the swastika.
One young woman and five men, all residents of northern Burlington County, also have been arrested. One was arrested at Cornell University, where he is a student.
Summons were issued to three other suspects.
Burlington County prosecutor Steve Raymond said that many of the victims had been afraid to come forward and that other crimes that were reported appeared to be random vandalism.

At a state house news conference with Raymond, Gov. Christie Whitman described the crime as the work of "bigoted cowards." She said that the victims suffered great harm, even though no one was physically injured.
"When people are afraid to go out of their houses at night they are harmed," she said.

Raymond said the suspects called themselves "The Crew" and were organised enough to have a hierarchy and assigned roles. Their alleged targets were nine black families living in the area. One victim, a 76-year-old grandmother, was harassed with almost daily telephone calls.
The group allegedly made racist phone calls, yelled racial slurs as they drove by victims' homes and threw eggs at their property.
